source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 3ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Ακεψιμάς, Ιωσήφ και Αειθαλάς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 3 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: «Ο Άγιος Ακεψιμάς ήταν επίσκοπος», martyred under Shapur II. A `dates` object is proposed from the page's «περί το 330 μ.Χ.» where the folder had none. The entry enumerates three men: Joseph is an upgrade in this same file, and Aithalas is reported and not touched because his folder already carries a venerated Greek row on 2 September. **The same day's listing keeps a second Acepsimas**, a hermit of the fourth century who died in peace, who is a new folder of this batch and not this bishop. The apolytikion names all three and is taken; the kontakion names this Acepsimas «σὺν τοῖς συνάθλοις σου» and is taken into his folder only; the page's «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον» is the common of martyrs, «Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου, Κύριε», and the Κάθισμα is neither a troparion nor a kontakion, and neither is drafted. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, Troparul Sfinților Sfințiți Mucenici Achepsima episcopul, Iosif preotul și Aitala diaconul, Glasul 4

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contests received incorruptible crowns from Thee our God; for possessing Thy strength they overthrew their torturers, and broke the feeble daring of the demons. By their prayers save Thou our souls, O Christ God.

hymns.text: Ὡς θεράποντες, τῆς εὐσέβειας, στῦλοι ὤφθητε, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, πυρσολατρῶν καθελόντες τὸ φρύαγμα, Ἀκεψιμᾶ Ἱεράρχα πολύαθλε, Ἀειθαλᾶ Ἰωσὴφ τὲ μακάριοι. Ἀλλ' αἰτήσασθε, Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν πανεύφημοι, δωρήσασθαι ἠμὶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Ακεψιμάς, Ιωσήφ και Αειθαλάς». It names all three of them and no other saint, and calls this Acepsimas Ἱεράρχα. The page's second apolytikion is the common of martyrs and is not taken.

english.text: As servants of godliness you were shown to be pillars of the Church, pulling down the arrogance of the fire-worshippers — Acepsimas the much-contending hierarch, and blessed Aithalas and Joseph. All-praised ones, ask Christ our God to grant us his great mercy.

hymns.text: Τὰ θεῖα σοφέ, σεπτῶς ἐμυσταγώγησας, θυσία δεκτὴ ἐγένου Παμμακάριστε· τοῦ Χριστοῦ γὰρ ἔπιες, τὸ ποτήριον ἐνδόξως Ἅγιε, Ἀκεψιμᾶ σὺν τοῖς συνάθλοις σου, πρεσβεύων ἀπαύστως ὑπὲρ πάντων ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — on the page of «Άγιοι Ακεψιμάς, Ιωσήφ και Αειθαλάς». It names him alone and calls his companions only «τοῖς συνάθλοις σου», so it is taken into his folder and not into theirs.

english.text: You brought men reverently into the divine mysteries, wise one, and became an acceptable sacrifice, all-blessed; for you drank the cup of Christ gloriously, holy Acepsimas, with your fellow contenders, interceding without ceasing for us all.

death.note: saint.gr: «Και οι τρεις μαρτύρησαν για το Χριστό, όταν βασιλιάς της Περσίας ήταν ο Σαπώρ ο Β' (περί το 330 μ.Χ.)» — the page's own year, written «περί», about, for the reign it sets the martyrdom in. No year of birth is given.
